en.headline: Paul Chan says US trade policy impact on Hong Kong mainly psychological
en.dek: The Financial Secretary expressed cautious optimism for the second half, citing resilient exports and domestic demand after the government raised its full-year growth forecast.
body: Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po said on Sunday that changes in US trade policy and interest-rate trends would affect Hong Kong’s economy but the impact would be “primarily psychological”. He spoke on a radio programme two days after the government raised its 2026 GDP growth forecast to a range of 3.5 to 4.5 per cent.

Chan noted that the first half had been robust, driven by strong exports and resilient external and domestic demand. Retail sales had grown for 14 consecutive months and the catering sector showed mild improvement, while asset markets remained stable and employment healthy.

He said interest rates were expected to see little change for the rest of the year, with one further 0.25 percentage-point rise already priced in by markets. Risks linked to the US midterm elections were manageable. Hong Kong companies and mainland firms had shown agility in adapting to shifting trade conditions, and the US now ranked only fourth among the city’s export markets by volume.

zh.headline: 陳茂波：美國貿易政策對港影響主要屬心理層面
zh.dek: 財政司司長在電台節目表示，上半年經濟表現不俗，對下半年審慎樂觀，外部風險可控。
body: 財政司司長陳茂波周日在電台節目表示，美國貿易政策及息率走勢會影響香港經濟，但影響「主要屬心理層面」。政府日前已將2026年全年經濟增長預測上調至3.5%至4.5%。
他指上半年表現相當不錯，出口強勁，外部及內部需求均具韌性。零售銷售連續14個月增長，餐飲業亦有溫和改善，資產市場穩定，就業情況健康。
陳茂波預期年內息率變動不大，市場已消化再加息0.25厘的預期；美國中期選舉相關風險屬可控。他指出本港及內地企業過去數年已展現適應貿易環境變化的靈活性，美國現時僅為香港第四大出口市場。
